content.comment_body: Hello, Have you found a solution? I’m facing the same issue. Downloading with VPN via [product_name] works perfectly, but with [product_name] Web Editor, when I use the test function I receive an error: "IP addresses not in the same subnet." Thanks ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Split from [company_name] [product_name] Web Editor download using VPN.

Hi, As mentioned in another post: transferring a [product_name] Web Editor project to a [product_name] device only works within a local network and not remotely or through the Internet. Hope this helps.

Regardless of the reason for this issue (which may remain a [company_name] secret), there could be a workaround using L2TP or similar Layer 2 tunneling protocols. Placing a Raspberry Pi in the same network as the PLC could serve as a network endpoint, allowing your computer to join the correct subnet. However, be aware that IT administrators generally frown upon such setups.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having trouble with remote downloads over VPN when using [product_name] Web Editor, specifically encountering errors related to subnet mismatches. Remote downloads with [product_name] Soft Comfort operate smoothly, but [product_name] Web Editor restricts downloads to local networks, causing frustration for those needing remote access and configuration. Users desire uniform network support across [company_name] software tools and view local-only limitations as a barrier.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like [product_name] Web Editor to support remote downloads via VPN in a way that matches [product_name] Soft Comfort, enabling workflows that involve remote network access outside of local environments.
